Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: There is evidence of online payments in port community systems: Djibouti Port Community Systems (DPCS) has online payments integrated with multiple banks, with 11% of port community transactions already paid online (this is a form of B2G/P2G-like payments to port/public systems but not explicit tax payments). No primary evidence found for nationwide tax P2G payments yet; Smart Wallet is described as intended to support tax payments in future. ([Developing Telecoms](https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/financial-services/15938-digital-money-transfer-system-comes-to-djibouti-s-ports.html);[CoinGeek](https://coingeek.com/libya-expands-digital-payments-djibouti-launches-e-wallet/))

Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Djibouti adopted a comprehensive Digital Code (approved June 30, 2025) which includes personal data protection provisions, establishing a general data protection regime (not specific to payment data). ([Ecofin Agency](https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0107-47508-djibouti-introduces-digital-code-to-structure-its-digital-ecosystem);[Jones Day](https://www.jonesday.com/en/insights/2025/07/national-assembly-of-the-republic-of-djibouti-approves-digital-code))

Definition: Whether payment system governance explicitly includes mechanisms to ensure inclusivity and represent interests of vulnerable populations, including provisions for input from all participant types, consumer representatives, small providers, or explicit financial inclusion mandates in governance documents.
Comments: AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022 shows SYRAD does not meet the “pro-poor governance” criterion in its inclusivity assessment table (criterion not checked for SYRAD), and no public evidence was found of end-user/consumer representation or explicit inclusion mandate in SYRAD governance. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/EN_SIIPS_Report_web.pdf))

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Djibouti has a domestic instant payment system called SYRAD (Système de Règlement Automatisé de Djibouti), which AfricaNenda’s SIIPS 2022 report lists as launched in 2022 and live/active as of June 2022; however, SIIPS 2024 executive summary states SYRAD is “not fully operational,” suggesting partial deployment rather than fully nationwide operation. ([AfricaNenda SIIPS 2022](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/EN_SIIPS_Report_web.pdf);[AfricaNenda SIIPS 2024 Executive Summary](https://www.africanenda.org/uploads/files/siips_2024_executive_summary_en-2.pdf))
